objects.definition: struct pair_first_construct_t {};
objects.description: Tag type used to disambiguate the single-first-element constructor of eastl::pair. Constructing pair(pair_first_construct_t, first_value) initializes first with first_value and default-constructs second. No state; trivially constructible/destructible.

Non-templated doubly-linked circular list node base used as the anchor/sentinel and to support allocator-agnostic node operations (insert/remove/splice/reverse/swap). Holds prev/next pointers but no payload value.

objects.definition: static EA_CONSTEXPR size_t dynamic_extent = size_t(-1);
objects.description: Constant sentinel value used by eastl::span to represent a dynamic (unknown at compile time) extent. It aliases the built-in size_t constant placed in the eastl namespace.

SFINAE-friendly type trait that evaluates to true_type if a type supports eastl::size(x) and eastl::data(x); otherwise false_type. Used internally by span constructors to enable conversions from generic containers.
Compile-time integral_constant that computes the extent of a subspan given an original extent, offset, and count. Used to form the correct span type in subspan().
Type trait that detects whether a type is an eastl::array<T, N> specialization for element type T. Used to control span constructors.
Internal storage helper for span. For static extent, stores only pointer and encodes size in the type; for dynamic extent, stores pointer and runtime size. Not intended for external use.

Non-owning view over a contiguous sequence of elements of type T with either static or dynamic extent. Provides bounds-checked access in debug via assertions, iterator support, and subview creation (first, last, subspan). Construction is from pointer+size, pointer range, C arrays, eastl::array, compatible containers exposing data() and size(), or convertible span. Does not manage lifetime of underlying data.
A sink type whose assignment operator ignores any assigned value. A single static instance eastl::ignore is provided for tie/structured binding patterns.

objects.definition: struct nullopt_tag_t {};
objects.description: Tag type used solely to disambiguate construction of eastl::nullopt_t. It carries no data and has no behavior.
Sentinel type representing the disengaged/empty state for eastl::optional. A single constexpr instance eastl::nullopt is defined for use in code (e.g., optional<T> o = eastl::nullopt;).

objects.definition: struct monostate {};
objects.description: Unit/empty type intended as a well-behaved empty alternative for variant to enable default-constructibility or represent an empty state.
Hash function object specialization for eastl::monostate. Returns a fixed hash value.

Type-erased container for a single value of any copy-constructible type. Uses a small-buffer optimization (SBO) with an internal union to store small nothrow-move-constructible types in-place; otherwise allocates externally. Provides construction from arbitrary values, in-place construction via in_place_type_t, copy/move semantics, reset/swap, has_value, optional RTTI-based type(), and type-safe retrieval via any_cast plus unsafe_any_cast. Lifetime is managed via a per-contained-type handler function that performs get/destroy/copy/move/type_info operations.
Hash functor specialization computing an FNV-like hash for eastl::string_view over bytes.
Conditional hash specialization for u8string_view when char8_t is a distinct type. Uses FNV-like byte hash.
Hash functor specialization for u16string_view; hashes 16-bit code units with an FNV-like algorithm.
Hash functor specialization for u32string_view; hashes 32-bit code units with an FNV-like algorithm.
Conditional hash functor specialization for wstring_view when wchar_t is a distinct UTF type; hashes code units using an FNV-like algorithm.

objects.definition: typedef basic_string_view<char32_t> u32string_view;

A templated, EASTL-specific implementation of a dynamically sized string similar to std::basic_string, with small-string optimization (SSO), custom allocator support, and numerous extensions (sprintf helpers, trim/make_lower/upper, detach, set_capacity/force_size, transparent comparisons). Nested helper structs model the internal layout and tag types for special constructors.
Transparent hash aggregator for narrow string-related types (char and optionally char8_t). Provides overloaded operator() from internal base(s) and marks is_transparent for heterogeneous lookup.
Transparent hash aggregator for UTF-16 strings (and wchar_t when it is 16-bit), enabling heterogeneous hashing of pointers, basic_string, and string_view forms.
Transparent hash aggregator for UTF-32 strings (and wchar_t when it is 32-bit), providing heterogeneous hashing across pointer, basic_string, and string_view inputs.
Transparent hash aggregator centered on wchar_t strings and, when wchar_t aliases UTF-16/32, also includes the corresponding char16_t/char32_t overloads for heterogeneous lookup.

Doubly-linked intrusive node to embed in user objects. Each node carries next/prev pointers and can be linked into an eastl intrusive_list ring anchored by a sentinel. When EASTL_VALIDATE_INTRUSIVE_LIST is enabled, ctor/dtor assert correct linkage state.
Non-templated base for intrusive_list providing the sentinel anchor node and core ring-manipulation utilities (empty/size/clear/pop/reverse/validate). Manages no allocation; nodes are user-owned.
Enumeration describing floating-point rounding modes used by eastl::numeric_limits specializations.
Enumeration describing whether a floating-point type supports IEEE denormalized (subnormal) values.

functions.name: eastl::integral_constant::operator value_type
functions.signature:
template <typename T, T v>
EA_CONSTEXPR eastl::integral_constant<T, v>::operator typename eastl::integral_constant<T, v>::value_type() const EA_NOEXCEPT
functions.description: Conversion operator that returns the stored compile-time constant as a value of value_type. Typically used to obtain the boolean/integral value of a type trait in constant expressions or as a runtime value. constexpr and noexcept; no side effects.
requirements: Must be invoked on a valid eastl::integral_constant<T, v> object (usually via the type itself or a derived alias such as true_type/false_type).
No arguments; can be used in constant expressions. There are no additional preconditions stated.

functions.name: eastl::integral_constant::operator()
functions.signature:
template <typename T, T v>
EA_CONSTEXPR typename eastl::integral_constant<T, v>::value_type
eastl::integral_constant<T, v>::operator()() const EA_NOEXCEPT
functions.description: Function-call operator that returns the stored compile-time constant as a value of value_type. Provides a callable interface to integral_constant instances. constexpr and noexcept; no side effects.
requirements: Must be invoked on a valid eastl::integral_constant<T, v> object (or aliases like true_type/false_type).
No arguments; can be used in constant expressions. There are no additional preconditions stated.

functions.name: eastl::declval
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
typename eastl::add_rvalue_reference<T>::type eastl::declval() EA_NOEXCEPT;
functions.description: Utility that yields an rvalue reference to T (T&&) in unevaluated contexts, enabling use of T's members in decltype and similar expressions without constructing an object. Declared only; intentionally has no definition and must never be evaluated.
requirements: Must be used only in unevaluated contexts (e.g., inside decltype, sizeof, alignof, or as operand to noexcept).
Must not be odr-used, invoked, or evaluated at runtime; there is no definition by design.
Template parameter T may be any type; no construction requirements are imposed because the function is never evaluated.

functions.name: eastl::unwrap_iterator
functions.signature:
template <typename Iterator>
EASTL_REMOVE_AT_2024_SEPT inline typename eastl::is_iterator_wrapper_helper<Iterator, eastl::is_iterator_wrapper<Iterator>::value>::iterator_type unwrap_iterator(Iterator it)
functions.description: Unwraps a single layer of an iterator wrapper and returns the underlying iterator type; if the passed type is not a wrapper, returns it unchanged. Intended for wrappers like move_iterator, generic_iterator, or reverse_iterator-wrapped wrappers. Returns by value.
requirements: Iterator may be a wrapper type exposing unwrap(); otherwise it is returned as-is.
Only unwraps one layer; callers must invoke repeatedly to peel multiple wrapper layers.
Argument it must be a valid iterator object per its underlying semantics.

functions.description: Equality comparison for reverse_iterator adaptors. Compares underlying base iterators for equality.
requirements: a.base() and b.base() must be comparable for equality.
Both reverse iterators should be from compatible underlying iterator/range types.

requirements: a.base() and b.base() must be comparable for equality.
Both move iterators should be compatible.

requirements: Underlying base iterators must support operator>.

functions.name: eastl::operator-
functions.signature:
template <typename Iterator1, typename Iterator2>
EA_CPP14_CONSTEXPR inline typename eastl::reverse_iterator<Iterator1>::difference_type operator-(const eastl::reverse_iterator<Iterator1>& a, const eastl::reverse_iterator<Iterator2>& b)
functions.description: Computes distance between two reverse_iterators as b.base() - a.base().

requirements: Underlying base iterators must support subtraction (typically random access).
Iterators must be from the same sequence or compatible ranges.

functions.name: eastl::operator+
functions.signature:
template <typename Iterator>
EA_CPP14_CONSTEXPR inline eastl::reverse_iterator<Iterator> operator+(typename eastl::reverse_iterator<Iterator>::difference_type n, const eastl::reverse_iterator<Iterator>& a)
functions.description: Adds an offset to a reverse_iterator returning a new iterator positioned n steps earlier in the underlying sequence (a.base() - n).
requirements: Underlying base iterator must support random-access addition/subtraction.
n may be negative only if Iterator’s arithmetic supports it (difference_type).

functions.name: eastl::make_move_if_noexcept_iterator

template <typename Iterator, typename IteratorType = typename eastl::conditional<eastl::is_nothrow_move_constructible<typename eastl::iterator_traits<Iterator>::value_type>::value || !eastl::is_copy_constructible<typename eastl::iterator_traits<Iterator>::value_type>::value, eastl::move_iterator<Iterator>, Iterator>::type>
inline IteratorType make_move_if_noexcept_iterator(Iterator i)

requirements: Iterator must be a valid iterator over a type with well-formed iterator_traits.

functions.name: eastl::distance

functions.name: eastl::align
functions.signature: void* eastl::align(size_t alignment, size_t size, void*& ptr, size_t& space)
functions.description: C++11-like align: if there is enough space in the buffer [ptr, ptr + space) to fit size bytes aligned to alignment, adjusts ptr to the aligned address, reduces space by the consumed padding, and returns the aligned pointer; otherwise returns NULL and leaves ptr and space unchanged.
requirements: ptr must point to the start of a buffer of length space bytes.
alignment should be a power of two (as per std::align semantics).
If space < size or no suitably aligned region fits, returns NULL and does not modify ptr/space.

functions.name: eastl::align_advance
functions.signature: void* eastl::align_advance(size_t alignment, size_t size, void* ptr, size_t space, void** ptrAdvanced = NULL, size_t* spaceReduced = NULL)
functions.description: Extension similar to align that returns the aligned pointer without modifying the provided ptr/space directly, but can optionally output the advanced pointer (aligned address + size) and remaining space via ptrAdvanced and spaceReduced.
requirements: ptr must point to the start of a buffer of length space bytes.
alignment should be a power of two (as per std::align semantics).
If space < size or no suitably aligned region fits, returns NULL and does not write outputs.

functions.name: eastl::pointer_traits::pointer_to
functions.signature:
template <typename Pointer>
static typename eastl::pointer_traits<Pointer>::pointer eastl::pointer_traits<Pointer>::pointer_to(typename eastl::conditional<eastl::is_void<typename eastl::pointer_traits<Pointer>::element_type>::value, void, typename eastl::pointer_traits<Pointer>::element_type>::type& r)
functions.description: Customization point that forwards to Pointer::pointer_to(r). For fancy pointer types, constructs a pointer to the referenced element r.
requirements: Pointer must provide static pointer Pointer::pointer_to(element_type&) and satisfy pointer_traits requirements (element_type, etc.).
If element_type is void, the exact type of r is unspecified per standard, but the call must be valid for the pointer type.

functions.name: eastl::pointer_traits<T*>::pointer_to
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
static T* eastl::pointer_traits<T*>::pointer_to(typename eastl::conditional<eastl::is_void<T>::value, void, T>::type& r) noexcept
functions.description: Specialization for raw pointers: returns addressof(r).
requirements: If T is not void, r must be a valid lvalue of type T.
For (cv-)void element types, the parameter type is unspecified per standard but must be acceptable to addressof semantics.

functions.name: eastl::to_address
functions.signature:
template <class T>
EA_CPP14_CONSTEXPR T* eastl::to_address(T* p) noexcept
functions.description: Returns the same pointer p for raw pointers, with a static_assert that T is not a function type.
requirements: T must not be a function type (enforced by static_assert).
p may be null; no dereference occurs.

functions.name: eastl::swap
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
inline void swap(T& a, T& b) EA_NOEXCEPT_IF(eastl::is_nothrow_move_constructible<T>::value && eastl::is_nothrow_move_assignable<T>::value)
functions.description: Swaps the values of two objects by move-constructing a temporary from a, assigning b into a, then the temporary into b. Intended general-purpose swap used by other algorithms and ADL. Prefer letting ADL find user-defined swaps when appropriate.
requirements: T must be MoveConstructible and MoveAssignable (the implementation moves a into a temporary, assigns b to a, and the temp to b).
If relying on the noexcept guarantee, T must be nothrow move-constructible and nothrow move-assignable.

functions.name: eastl::swap
functions.signature:
template <typename T, size_t N>
inline void swap(T (&a)[N], T (&b)[N]) EA_NOEXCEPT_IF(eastl::is_nothrow_swappable<T>::value)
functions.description: Swaps two same-sized C-style arrays element-wise using swap_ranges. Provides a convenience overload for arrays.
requirements: Arrays a and b must have the same element type T and the same bound N.
T must be swappable (element-wise swap is performed).
Noexcept only if T is nothrow swappable.

functions.name: eastl::iter_swap
functions.signature:
template <typename ForwardIterator1, typename ForwardIterator2>
inline void iter_swap(ForwardIterator1 a, ForwardIterator2 b)
functions.description: Swaps the values referred to by iterators a and b. Uses swap(*a, *b) when possible (same value/reference types), otherwise performs a manual move-based swap.
requirements: a and b must be valid iterators referring to dereferenceable elements.
The expressions *a and *b must be swappable; for the manual path, value_type of a must be MoveConstructible and both referenced elements must be MoveAssignable.
If the two iterator value/reference types are identical, swap(*a, *b) must be valid.

functions.name: eastl::swap_ranges
functions.signature:
template <typename ForwardIterator1, typename ForwardIterator2>
inline ForwardIterator2 swap_ranges(ForwardIterator1 first1, ForwardIterator1 last1, ForwardIterator2 first2)
functions.description: Swaps each element in [first1, last1) with the corresponding element starting at first2. Returns the end iterator of the second range (first2 + (last1 - first1)).
requirements: The range [first1, last1) must be a valid range.
The two ranges [first1, last1) and [first2, first2 + (last1 - first1)) shall not overlap (as stated in the comments).
Elements referred to by the iterators must be swappable.

functions.name: eastl::exchange
functions.signature:
template <typename T, typename U = T>
inline T exchange(T& obj, U&& new_value)
functions.description: Replaces obj with new_value (forwarded) and returns the old value of obj by move. Mirrors std::exchange.
requirements: T must be MoveConstructible (to return the old value) and Assignable from U (obj = forward<U>(new_value) must be valid).

functions.name: eastl::as_const
functions.signature:
template <class T>
EA_CONSTEXPR typename eastl::add_const<T>::type& as_const(T& t) EA_NOEXCEPT
functions.description: Casts an lvalue T& to const T&. Useful for invoking const overloads on non-const objects. Mirrors std::as_const.
requirements: t must be an lvalue of type T.
Returns a const reference; the caller must not attempt to modify through the returned reference.

functions.name: eastl::rel_ops::operator!=
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
inline bool operator!=(const T& x, const T& y)

requirements: A valid operator==(const T&, const T&) must be available.
Include or use the namespace eastl::rel_ops for ADL/lookup to find this operator where needed.

functions.name: eastl::rel_ops::operator>
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
inline bool operator>(const T& x, const T& y)
functions.description: Generates operator> in terms of y < x. Part of relational-operators helpers in eastl::rel_ops.
requirements: A valid operator<(const T&, const T&) must be available.
Bring eastl::rel_ops into scope to enable these operators.

functions.name: eastl::rel_ops::operator<=
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
inline bool operator<=(const T& x, const T& y)
functions.description: Generates operator<= in terms of !(y < x). Part of relational-operators helpers in eastl::rel_ops.
requirements: A valid operator<(const T&, const T&) must be available.
Bring eastl::rel_ops into scope to enable these operators.

functions.name: eastl::rel_ops::operator>=
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
inline bool operator>=(const T& x, const T& y)
functions.description: Generates operator>= in terms of !(x < y). Part of relational-operators helpers in eastl::rel_ops.
requirements: A valid operator<(const T&, const T&) must be available.
Bring eastl::rel_ops into scope to enable these operators.

functions.name: eastl::cmp_equal
functions.signature:
template <typename T, typename U>
EA_CONSTEXPR bool cmp_equal(const T x, const U y) EA_NOEXCEPT
functions.description: Safely compares two integral values of possibly different signedness for equality without unintended sign conversions. Mirrors std::cmp_equal.
requirements: Available only when EA_COMPILER_CPP17_ENABLED is defined in this header.
T and U must be integral types and not bool or char (enforced by static_asserts).

functions.name: eastl::cmp_not_equal
functions.signature:
template <typename T, typename U>
EA_CONSTEXPR bool cmp_not_equal(const T x, const U y) EA_NOEXCEPT
functions.description: Logical negation of cmp_equal; returns true if x and y are not equal with safe mixed-signedness handling.
requirements: Available only when EA_COMPILER_CPP17_ENABLED is defined.
T and U must be integral types and not bool or char.

functions.name: eastl::cmp_less
functions.signature:
template <typename T, typename U>
EA_CONSTEXPR bool cmp_less(const T x, const U y) EA_NOEXCEPT
functions.description: Safely compares whether x < y for integral types of possibly different signedness. Mirrors std::cmp_less.
requirements: Available only when EA_COMPILER_CPP17_ENABLED is defined.
T and U must be integral types and not bool or char.

functions.name: eastl::cmp_greater
functions.signature:
template <typename T, typename U>
EA_CONSTEXPR bool cmp_greater(const T x, const U y) EA_NOEXCEPT
functions.description: Returns cmp_less(y, x), providing safe mixed-signedness greater-than comparison for integral types.
requirements: Available only when EA_COMPILER_CPP17_ENABLED is defined.
T and U must be integral types and not bool or char.

functions.name: eastl::cmp_less_equal
functions.signature:
template <typename T, typename U>
EA_CONSTEXPR bool cmp_less_equal(const T x, const U y) EA_NOEXCEPT
functions.description: Returns !cmp_greater(x, y); safe mixed-signedness less-than-or-equal comparison for integral types.
requirements: Available only when EA_COMPILER_CPP17_ENABLED is defined.
T and U must be integral types and not bool or char.

functions.name: eastl::cmp_greater_equal
functions.signature:
template <typename T, typename U>
EA_CONSTEXPR bool cmp_greater_equal(const T x, const U y) EA_NOEXCEPT
functions.description: Returns !cmp_less(x, y); safe mixed-signedness greater-than-or-equal comparison for integral types.
requirements: Available only when EA_COMPILER_CPP17_ENABLED is defined.
T and U must be integral types and not bool or char.

functions.name: eastl::in_range
functions.signature:
template <typename T, typename U>
EA_CONSTEXPR bool in_range(const U x) EA_NOEXCEPT
functions.description: Checks whether integral value x lies within the inclusive range [numeric_limits<T>::min(), numeric_limits<T>::max()] with safe mixed-signedness logic. Mirrors std::in_range.
requirements: Available only when EA_COMPILER_CPP17_ENABLED is defined.
T and U must be integral types and not bool or char.

functions.name: eastl::make_pair
functions.signature:
template <typename T1, typename T2>
EA_CPP14_CONSTEXPR inline eastl::pair<typename eastl::remove_reference_wrapper<typename eastl::decay<T1>::type>::type,
                                       typename eastl::remove_reference_wrapper<typename eastl::decay<T2>::type>::type>
make_pair(T1&& a, T2&& b)
functions.description: Creates an eastl::pair by deducing element types from a and b (after decay and removing reference_wrapper). Convenience function similar to std::make_pair.
requirements: The deduced pair element types must be constructible from a and b respectively via forwarding.
Note: Reference wrappers are unwrapped; arrays/decay rules apply as with decay<T>.

functions.name: eastl::make_pair_ref
functions.signature:

make_pair_ref(T1&& a, T2&& b)
functions.description: Deprecated alias of make_pair (per comment in code). Constructs a pair with the same deduction/unwrapping rules as make_pair.
requirements: Same construction requirements as make_pair.
Marked with EASTL_REMOVE_AT_2024_SEPT; avoid for new code.

functions.name: eastl::get
functions.signature:

EA_CONSTEXPR const T1& get(const eastl::pair<T1, T2>& p) EA_NOEXCEPT

functions.name: eastl::operator==

EA_CPP14_CONSTEXPR inline bool operator==(const eastl::pair<T1, T2>& a, const eastl::pair<T1, T2>& b)

requirements: operator== must be valid for T1 and for T2 (used by the implementation).

EA_CPP14_CONSTEXPR inline bool operator>(const eastl::pair<T1, T2>& a, const eastl::pair<T1, T2>& b)

requirements: operator< must be valid for T1 and for T2.

requirements: operator< must be valid for T1 and for T2.

functions.name: eastl::operator<=>
functions.signature:

EA_CONSTEXPR inline std::common_comparison_category_t<synth_three_way_result<T1>, synth_three_way_result<T2>> operator<=>(const eastl::pair<T1, T2>& a, const eastl::pair<T1, T2>& b)

Three-way comparison via synth_three_way{}(first, first) and synth_three_way{}(second, second) must be valid for T1 and T2.

functions.name: eastl::validate_equal_to
functions.signature:
template <typename T, typename Compare>
bool eastl::validate_equal_to(const T& a, const T& b, Compare compare)
functions.description: Checks that a provided equality comparator is symmetric for the given arguments. It invokes compare(a, b) and compare(b, a) and returns whether the two results compare equal using operator==. Use to validate custom equality predicates.
requirements: T must be the same type for a and b and must be acceptable to Compare.
Compare must be callable as compare(const T&, const T&).
The return type of Compare must support operator== and be comparable for equality (typically bool).
compare(a, b) and compare(b, a) must be valid and side-effect-safe if used for validation.

functions.name: eastl::validate_not_equal_to
functions.signature:
template <typename T, typename Compare>
bool eastl::validate_not_equal_to(const T& a, const T& b, Compare compare)
functions.description: Validates that a provided inequality comparator yields consistent results in both argument orders. It calls compare(a, b) and compare(b, a) and returns whether the two results are equal using operator==. Intended for testing not-equal predicates.
requirements: T must be the same type for a and b and must be acceptable to Compare.
Compare must be callable as compare(const T&, const T&).
The return type of Compare must support operator== and be comparable for equality (typically bool).
compare(a, b) and compare(b, a) must be valid and side-effect-safe if used for validation.

functions.name: eastl::validate_greater
functions.signature:
template <typename T, typename Compare>
bool eastl::validate_greater(const T& a, const T& b, Compare compare)
functions.description: Checks a strict-ordering-style comparator (e.g., greater) for anti-symmetry on the given arguments. Returns !compare(a,b) || !compare(b,a), i.e., it fails only if both directions report a > b and b > a.
requirements: T must be the same type for a and b and must be acceptable to Compare.
Compare must be callable as compare(const T&, const T&) and be contextually convertible to bool.
compare(a, b) and compare(b, a) must be valid and side-effect-safe if used for validation.

functions.name: eastl::validate_less
functions.signature:
template <typename T, typename Compare>
bool eastl::validate_less(const T& a, const T& b, Compare compare)
functions.description: Checks a strict-ordering-style comparator (e.g., less) for anti-symmetry on the given arguments. Returns !compare(a,b) || !compare(b,a), i.e., it fails only if both directions report a < b and b < a.
requirements: T must be the same type for a and b and must be acceptable to Compare.
Compare must be callable as compare(const T&, const T&) and be contextually convertible to bool.
compare(a, b) and compare(b, a) must be valid and side-effect-safe if used for validation.

functions.name: eastl::validate_greater_equal
functions.signature:
template <typename T, typename Compare>
bool eastl::validate_greater_equal(const T& a, const T& b, Compare compare)
functions.description: Checks a non-strict comparator (e.g., greater_equal) for consistency on the given arguments. Returns !compare(a,b) || !compare(b,a), ensuring both directions are not simultaneously true.
requirements: T must be the same type for a and b and must be acceptable to Compare.
Compare must be callable as compare(const T&, const T&) and be contextually convertible to bool.
compare(a, b) and compare(b, a) must be valid and side-effect-safe if used for validation.

functions.name: eastl::validate_less_equal
functions.signature:
template <typename T, typename Compare>
bool eastl::validate_less_equal(const T& a, const T& b, Compare compare)
functions.description: Checks a non-strict comparator (e.g., less_equal) for consistency on the given arguments. Returns !compare(a,b) || !compare(b,a), ensuring both directions are not simultaneously true.
requirements: T must be the same type for a and b and must be acceptable to Compare.
Compare must be callable as compare(const T&, const T&) and be contextually convertible to bool.
compare(a, b) and compare(b, a) must be valid and side-effect-safe if used for validation.

functions.name: eastl::not_fn
functions.signature:
template <class F>
inline eastl::not_fn_ret<F> eastl::not_fn(F&& f)
functions.description: Wraps a callable f and returns a functor that negates f’s result on invocation. The returned object stores a decay_t<F> and forwards arguments to eastl::invoke, then applies operator! to the result. Use to invert predicates or callables producing a value negatable by operator!.
requirements: F must be constructible into decay_t<F> from F&& (copy/move as needed).
For any call operator used, eastl::invoke(decay_t<F>[& or &&], Args&&...) must be well-formed.
The result of the invoke must be valid with unary operator! and contextually convertible to bool.
If f holds references or pointers, the caller must ensure their lifetimes outlive uses of the returned functor.

functions.name: eastl::internal::floating_point_hash
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
size_t eastl::internal::floating_point_hash(T val)
functions.description: Hashes a floating-point value into size_t with -0.0 normalized to 0.0. Internally casts the value to a floating type whose size matches size_t (float or double) and bit-casts its representation to size_t. Used by eastl::hash<float>, eastl::hash<double>, and eastl::hash<long double>.
requirements: T must be a floating-point type convertible to float or double (the chosen size_t-sized floating type).
Comparison against -0.0 and the cast to the size_t-sized floating type must be well-formed for T.
No NaN canonicalization is performed; distinct NaN payloads that convert to the same intermediate representation will collide.

functions.description: Accumulates values in the range [first, last) into init using operator+= (i.e., init += *it) in order, returning the final accumulated value. Equivalent in purpose to std::accumulate’s three-parameter overload.
requirements: [first, last) must denote a valid input iterator range; each iterator must be incrementable and dereferenceable until last.
The value type of InputIterator must be addable to T with operator+= (or T must support operator+(T, value_type) semantically).
init must be a valid T and remain valid for successive += operations.
No overflow or domain checking is performed; behavior follows the underlying operators.

functions.name: eastl::iota
functions.signature:
template <typename ForwardIterator, typename T>
void eastl::iota(ForwardIterator first, ForwardIterator last, T value);
functions.description: Fills the range [first, last) with sequentially increasing values starting at value by repeatedly assigning *it = value and then ++value. Matches std::iota semantics.
requirements: [first, last) must denote a valid forward-iterator range; each position must be writable.
T must be convertible to ForwardIterator's value_type (assignment *it = value must be well-formed).
The expression ++value must be well-formed for T.
Exactly (last - first) assignments and increments are performed; ensure the output range has that capacity.

functions.name: eastl::inner_product
functions.signature:
template <typename InputIterator1, typename InputIterator2, typename T>
T eastl::inner_product(InputIterator1 first1, InputIterator1 last1, InputIterator2 first2, T init);
functions.description: Computes the inner (dot) product of two ranges starting with init by repeatedly doing init += (*first1 * *first2) while advancing both iterators in lockstep. Processes elements in order and returns the final accumulated value.
requirements: [first1, last1) must denote a valid input iterator range; first2 must refer to a range with at least as many readable elements as [first1, last1).
The expressions (*first1 * *first2) and init += (that product) must be well-formed; the product must be compatible with accumulation into T.
Dereferencing and incrementing both iterators must be valid for the entire range length.
No bounds checks are performed; it is the caller’s responsibility that the second range is long enough.

functions.name: eastl::partial_sum
functions.signature:
template <typename InputIterator, typename OutputIterator>
OutputIterator eastl::partial_sum(InputIterator first, InputIterator last, OutputIterator result);
functions.description: Produces the running totals of the input range [first, last) using operator+= and writes them to the output starting at result. The first output equals the first input; each subsequent output is the sum of all inputs up to that position. Returns the iterator one past the last output element written.
requirements: [first, last) must be a valid input iterator range; each element must be readable.
result must be an output iterator capable of receiving the value_type results; it must point to a large enough writable destination for the number of inputs.
The input value_type must support copy construction and operator+= to accumulate successive values; assignment to *result must be well-formed.
If first == last, no output is written and result is returned unchanged.

functions.name: eastl::adjacent_difference
functions.signature:
template <typename InputIterator, typename OutputIterator>
OutputIterator eastl::adjacent_difference(InputIterator first, InputIterator last, OutputIterator result);
functions.description: Writes to result the adjacent differences of the input range [first, last) using operator-. The first output equals the first input; each subsequent output is current_input - previous_input. Returns the iterator one past the last output element written.
requirements: [first, last) must be a valid input iterator range; elements must be readable.
result must be a valid output iterator with capacity for (last - first) outputs.
The input value_type must support copy construction and operator-; assignment to *result must be well-formed.
If first == last, no output is written and result is returned unchanged.

functions.name: eastl::is_constant_evaluated
functions.signature: [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool eastl::is_constant_evaluated() noexcept;
functions.description: Returns true if called within a constant-evaluated context (constexpr evaluation), false otherwise. Wraps the compiler builtin __builtin_is_constant_evaluated(). Useful for writing code that behaves differently in constant-evaluation versus runtime.
requirements: Requires a C++20-capable compiler/standard library where __builtin_is_constant_evaluated is available (guarded by EA_COMPILER_CPP20_ENABLED).
No arguments; no side effects; may be used in constant expressions.

functions.name: eastl::isnan
functions.signature: [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool eastl::isnan(float f);
functions.description: Checks if the float argument is a NaN by testing f != f. Mirrors std::isnan behavior for float.
requirements: Takes any float; no preconditions.
Evaluating f != f on signaling NaNs in constant evaluation could be restricted by the compiler, but this function is intended for constexpr use.

functions.name: eastl::midpoint
functions.signature:
template <typename T, eastl::enable_if_t<eastl::is_arithmetic_v<T> && !eastl::is_same_v<eastl::remove_cv_t<T>, bool>, int> = 0>
constexpr T eastl::midpoint(T lhs, T rhs) noexcept;
functions.description: Computes the midpoint of two arithmetic values lhs and rhs without overflowing for integers and with at most one inexact operation for floating points. For integers, rounding is toward lhs when the sum is odd. Handles NaN propagation as documented in the implementation notes.
requirements: T must be an arithmetic type and not bool (enforced via enable_if).
For integral T, computation avoids overflow by difference/halving; inputs may be any representable T values.

For floating-point T, if evaluated at runtime and either argument is NaN, the function propagates NaN by performing lhs + rhs (raising FE_INVALID); during constant evaluation, a NaN argument is returned directly to avoid UB.
No side effects; callable in constant expressions under C++20.

functions.name: eastl::lerp
functions.signature: constexpr float eastl::lerp(float a, float b, float t) EA_NOEXCEPT;
functions.description: Computes linear interpolation/extrapolation between a and b as a + t * (b - a), with implementation guarding against certain rounding issues and preserving monotonicity as per P0811/Cpp20 lerp semantics.
requirements: Accepts any finite or infinite float values; works for t in any real value (interpolates for t in [0,1], extrapolates otherwise).
No exceptions; EA_NOEXCEPT per macro.

functions.name: eastl::synth_three_way::operator()
functions.description: Performs a synthesized three-way comparison between two values. If T and U satisfy std::three_way_comparable_with, it returns the result of t <=> u (a standard comparison category type, e.g., std::strong_ordering/weak_ordering/partial_ordering). Otherwise, it derives a std::weak_ordering by evaluating (t < u) and (u < t). Intended for use as a generic comparator that yields a three-way comparison result in C++20 code.
requirements: This operator is available only when EA_COMPILER_HAS_THREE_WAY_COMPARISON is defined and a C++20 compiler with three-way comparison support is used.
For the given T and U, the expressions (t < u) and (u < t) must be valid and each convertible to bool (per the requires-clause).
Arguments t and u must be valid objects bound to const references of types T and U, respectively.

If std::three_way_comparable_with<T, U> is satisfied, the expression t <=> u must be valid; the return type will be that expression’s comparison category type. Otherwise, the return type is std::weak_ordering.
No specific error handling is defined; the function has no side effects and returns a comparison category value.

Elements are immutable; do not attempt to modify through the returned pointer.

requirements: The std::initializer_list<E> object must be alive when called and for as long as the returned iterator is used; the iterator becomes invalid when the list's lifetime ends (typically end of the full expression).

Elements are immutable; do not attempt to modify through the returned pointer.

Elements are immutable; the returned pointer is const.

May be equal to std::begin(ilist) if the list is empty.

template <typename T, typename Order>
T eastl::atomic<T>::load(Order order) const;
functions.description: Atomically loads and returns the current value, applying the specified memory ordering. Valid orders for load are relaxed, acquire, and seq_cst. If T is a pointer type, read_depends is also valid and enforces address/data-dependency ordering suitable for pointer-chasing reads.
requirements: Valid memory orders for load are: relaxed, acquire, seq_cst.
Additionally, if T is a pointer type, memory_order_read_depends is allowed.

If using memory_order_read_depends, the returned pointer must only be used to subsequently read (dereference) memory; arithmetic with constant offsets, casting for intrusive/offset computations, and nullptr equality checks are allowed; using relational/equality operators other than nullptr checks to form control dependencies is forbidden.

functions.name: eastl::atomic::compare_exchange_weak
functions.signature:
template <typename T, typename Order>
bool eastl::atomic<T>::compare_exchange_weak(T& expected, T desired, Order successOrder, Order failOrder);
functions.description: Atomically compares the stored value with expected. If equal, replaces it with desired (RMW) and returns true; otherwise loads the observed value into expected (load) and returns false. The weak variant may fail spuriously even if equal, so it is typically used in a loop. successOrder applies to the RMW success path; failOrder applies to the load on failure.
requirements: failOrder cannot be stronger than successOrder.
On failure, the function writes the observed value into expected; callers must check the boolean return to determine success.
Use in a loop to handle spurious failure.

Valid memory orders are those accepted by the underlying success/failure paths: success path (RMW) supports all orders; failure path (load) supports relaxed, acquire, seq_cst (and read_depends for pointer types).
The atomic object must be initialized.

functions.description: Performs an atomic compare-and-exchange like the weak variant, but does not fail spuriously if the stored value equals expected. successOrder applies to the RMW success path; failOrder applies to the load on failure.
requirements: failOrder cannot be stronger than successOrder.
On failure, the function writes the observed value into expected; callers must check the boolean return.
Valid memory orders are those accepted by the underlying success/failure paths as described for the weak variant.
The atomic object must be initialized.

data_types.description: A generic byte buffer with no format constraints. May contain any 8-bit values, including NUL (0x00). Often supplied as a std::string where bytes are read individually or appended.

Text-like data passed to functions expecting const char* or string constructors. Although typically interpreted as UTF-8, the code paths accept any byte sequence, including embedded NULs when length-aware containers are used; however, when passed via c_str() to constructors taking const char*, content after the first NUL is ignored.

generators.generator:
import random
import os
import string
from typing import List

# We generate buffers intended for FUZZ_PARAM_STR uses across EASTL algorithm stubs.
# These stubs construct eastl::string and string_view from std::string data, sometimes
# pass c_str() (null-terminated) and sometimes use explicit size. We therefore:
# - Produce mostly printable UTF-8-like text with embedded edge cases
# - Include NULs and high-bytes to exercise equality/ordering/hash
# - Vary lengths to hit small/medium ranges used by stubs (up to ~1024),
#   but keep total <= 4096 bytes
# - Concatenate multiple independent strings separated by newlines so that each
#   FUZZ_PARAM_STR() call can consume a different slice from the same buffer
# Fuzzers typically split the single input buffer for multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls.

ASCII = string.ascii_letters + string.digits
PUNCT = "-_./:+@#%&*()[]{}|^~=?,;!$'\""
WHITES = " \t\r\n\v\f"

# A few interesting substrings to trigger behaviors (sorting, set algorithms, searches)
INTERESTING_SUBSTRINGS = [
    "",  # empty
    "a", "A", "0", "\n", "\t",
    "aaaaaa", "AAAAAA", "000000",
    "abc", "ABC", "abba", "racecar",
    # sequences with duplicates to exercise unique/remove
    "xxxxx", "yyzzzyy",
    # mixed cases and punctuation
    "EastL-TEST_v1.0",
    # NUL in the middle (only content before NUL seen via c_str())
    "bin\x00data",
    # ascending/descending for binary_search/lower_bound consistency
    "abcdefg", "gfedcba",
]

# Some byte patterns including non-ASCII
BYTE_PATTERNS: List[bytes] = [
    b"\x00", b"\xff", b"\x80\x81\xfe", b"\x00\x00\x00",
    b"\xc3\xa9" ,   # UTF-8 e'
    b"\xf0\x9f\x98\x80",  # 😀
]

def _rand_printable(r: random.Random, n: int) -> str:
    alphabet = ASCII + PUNCT + WHITES
    return ''.join(r.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))

def _with_nuls(r: random.Random, s: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Randomly inject a few NULs inside the buffer
    if not s:
        return b"\x00" if r.random() < 0.2 else s
    b = bytearray(s)
    inject = r.randint(0, max(1, len(b)//16))
    for _ in range(inject):
        pos = r.randrange(0, len(b))
        b[pos] = 0
    return bytes(b)

def _build_one_string(r: random.Random, target_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Construct a single interesting slice with mixed content
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    # Start with ASCII printable base
    base_len = max(0, target_len - r.randint(0, target_len//2))
    base = _rand_printable(r, base_len).encode('utf-8', 'ignore')
    parts.append(base)

    # Append 0-3 interesting substrings
    for _ in range(r.randint(0, 3)):
        s = r.choice(INTERESTING_SUBSTRINGS)
        parts.append(s.encode('utf-8', 'ignore'))

    # Append some raw bytes patterns occasionally
    for _ in range(r.randint(0, 2)):
        parts.append(r.choice(BYTE_PATTERNS))

    # Optionally ensure non-empty when desired
    data = b''.join(parts)

    # Optionally trim/extend to be around target_len
    if len(data) > 0 and r.random() < 0.6:
        # Shuffle to avoid predictable positions
        ba = bytearray(data)
        r.shuffle(ba)
        data = bytes(ba)

    # Adjust size to near target_len (but keep variety)
    if len(data) > target_len:
        # Keep head/tail mix
        cut_head = r.randint(0, min(len(data)//4, len(data)-target_len))
        data = data[cut_head:cut_head+target_len]
    elif len(data) < target_len and target_len <= 1024:
        pad = _rand_printable(r, target_len - len(data)).encode('utf-8', 'ignore')
        data += pad

    # Randomly inject NULs
    data = _with_nuls(r, data)

    # Sometimes ensure null-terminated for c_str() paths
    if r.random() < 0.5 and (not data or data[-1] != 0):
        data += b"\x00"

    return data


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide how many slices we want to provide; many stubs call FUZZ_PARAM_STR repeatedly.
    # Provide between 8 and 32 separate strings separated by newlines.
    count = r.randint(12, 24)

    # Choose a distribution of lengths, biased to small/medium with occasional larger slices
    lengths: List[int] = []
    for _ in range(count):
        p = r.random()
        if p < 0.55:
            lengths.append(r.randint(0, 64))
        elif p < 0.85:
            lengths.append(r.randint(65, 256))
        elif p < 0.97:
            lengths.append(r.randint(257, 1024))
        else:
            lengths.append(r.randint(1025, 1500))

    slices: List[bytes] = []
    for L in lengths:
        slices.append(_build_one_string(r, L))

    # Interleave with newlines as separators; include occasional empty line
    out_parts: List[bytes] = []
    for i, s in enumerate(slices):
        out_parts.append(s)
        # Add a newline separator (not NUL) to let the harness split easily
        if i != len(slices) - 1:
            # sometimes multiple newlines to create empty tokens
            nl_count = 1 + (1 if r.random() < 0.15 else 0)
            out_parts.append(b"\n" * nl_count)

    data = b''.join(out_parts)

    # Ensure overall size <= 4096
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]

    # Guarantee at least one non-empty printable prefix for functions that expect non-empty strings
    if not data:
        data = b"A\nB\n"

    return data
